# How the de-identification tools rank, and what decides whether an identifier is removed

<!-- generated by python/scripts/76_deid_drivers.py; do not edit -->

> **Fake PHI on synthetic notes** (the de-identification challenge set: seed 7, 400 notes, 2,714 identifiers, 2,462 dental decoys). Counts of what the tools did, read after the runs: they describe, they do not prove. Generated by `python/scripts/76_deid_drivers.py` from `data/deid/drivers/span_result.csv.gz` (a CPU rerun that reproduces `data/deid/scores.csv` exactly) and `data/deid/scores.csv`; tables in `data/datasets/model_drivers/deid_*.csv` and, on Databricks, `health_transformation_lab.gold_perio_bench.deid_*`.

The same format as [the note-reading models' page](model_drivers.md), applied to the [de-identification benchmark](deidentification.md): a ranked table with paired tests against the best tool; pairs of tools that differ in one ingredient, tested the same way; and which facts of an identifier and its note, and which ingredients of a tool, predict whether the identifier is removed, scored by AUC.

**In plain words.** A tool removes an identifier only if not one character of it survives. The best tool run here, **hf_stanford+hf_obi+regex_v2+guard**, removes 2,599 of 2,714 (95.8%) and cuts 1.7% of dental terms. Every other paired tool removes significantly fewer on the same identifiers (exact McNemar p < 0.05). What decides removal is mostly the identifier itself (its identifier category above all), then the tool (regex rules added (none to regex_v2) or extended (regex to regex_v2)).

## How the per-identifier results were made

`data/deid/scores.csv` holds aggregates only, so the paired tests below come from a rerun on CPU of every tool that runs locally (regex, regex_v2, Presidio with spaCy `en_core_web_lg`, the two Hugging Face models, their unions and the dental guard), on the same challenge set with the benchmark's own defaults (`python/scripts/76_deid_drivers.py --rerun`). The rerun reproduces the committed entity recall and decoy damage exactly in 60 of 60 tool-tier cells (table `deid_reproduction`). **ai_mask** (a Databricks SQL function) can't be rerun here: its rows come from the committed aggregates, with a Wilson interval, and are **not paired** (no McNemar p, no rank range).

## 1. The ranking

- **Removed**: identifiers with no character left, of 2,714 (95% CI: notes resampled, since identifiers in one note go together).
- **Rank**: the 95% range of the tool's rank among the paired tools over the same note resamples.
- **Leader only / tool only**: identifiers the leader removes and this tool leaks, and the reverse; the exact McNemar p is on these two counts (it treats identifiers as independent, so it is optimistic).
- **Unseen**: the held-out tier (identifier shapes added after regex_v2 was frozen): the fair comparison, since regex_v2 was written alongside the hard tier.
- **Decoy damage**: dental terms that look like PHI (Glickman class II, #19, 6-5-6, D4341) with any character cut: over-redaction. Lower is better.

|---:|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|

## 3. What decides whether an identifier is removed

Over all 40,710 tool-identifier runs (15 paired tools), a logistic regression predicts removal from the identifier's and its note's facts, the tool's ingredients, or both (out-of-fold AUC, folds and 95% bootstrap by note):

| Predictors | AUC (95% CI) |
|---|---|
| The identifier's and its note's facts alone | 0.83 (0.82 to 0.84) |
| The tool's ingredients alone | 0.73 (0.72 to 0.74) |
| Both | 0.91 (0.91 to 0.92) |

An additive fit can't credit an ingredient that helps only one kind of identifier (regex_v2 on formatted IDs, the models on names), so the tool's share is a floor. Leaving one group of predictors out of the full fit, the AUC lost ranks the drivers:

| Left out | Kind | AUC lost |
|---|---|---:|
| identifier category (HIPAA Safe Harbor / i2b2 2014) | identifier | 0.031 |
| regex rules added (none to regex_v2) or extended (regex to regex_v2) | tool | 0.025 |
| the note's tier (easy header shapes, hard prose shapes, unseen held-out shapes) | note | 0.019 |
| routed by identifier type | tool | 0.014 |
| hf_stanford added | tool | 0.011 |
| how the identifier is written (capitalised, all caps, lowercase, digits, letters and digits) | identifier | 0.004 |
| identifier length in words | identifier | 0.004 |
| hf_obi added | tool | 0.002 |
| Presidio added | tool | 0.002 |
| identifier length in characters | identifier | 0.002 |
| where in the note it sits | note | 0.000 |
| dental guard added | tool | 0.000 |
| identifiers in the note | note | 0.000 |

## Where this lives on Databricks

`python/scripts/77_load_deid_drivers.py` loads the tables above into `health_transformation_lab.gold_perio_bench`, each with a comment on the table and every column and the batch key (`run_id`, `run_ts`, `git_commit_sha`). Loading again replaces them.

| Table | One row per |
|---|---|
| `deid_tool_rank` | tool (ai_mask rows not paired) |
| `deid_reproduction` | rerun tool and tier: rerun against committed scores |
| `deid_contrast` | pair of tools differing in one ingredient |
| `deid_ingredient_effect` | ingredient |
| `deid_category_effect` | span kind, fact and level |
| `deid_driver_fit` | predictor set |
| `deid_driver_drop` | predictor group left out |
| `deid_span_result` | paired tool and labelled span (identifier or decoy): characters removed, leaked, damaged |

```sql
-- the identifiers the leader leaks, by category and tier
select category_code, tier_code, count(*) as leaked_count
from health_transformation_lab.gold_perio_bench.deid_span_result
where method_code = 'hf_stanford+hf_obi+regex_v2+guard' and is_leaked group by all order by leaked_count desc;
```
